questions.stem: What is the relative charge of a neutron?
questions.explanation: Neutrons have no charge (relative charge of 0). They are found in the nucleus alongside positively charged protons.

options.text: Because the number of protons equals the number of electrons, so positive and negative charges balance
Because they contain neutrons which cancel out all charges
Because protons and neutrons have the same charge

questions.explanation: In a neutral atom, the number of protons (+1 each) equals the number of electrons (-1 each), so the positive and negative charges cancel out to give an overall charge of zero.

questions.stem: What is the relative mass of an electron?
questions.explanation: An electron has a relative mass of approximately 1/1836, which is so small it is often considered negligible. This is why almost all of an atom's mass is concentrated in the nucleus.

questions.stem: An atom of sodium has an atomic number of 11 and a mass number of 23. How many neutrons does it contain?
questions.explanation: Neutrons = Mass number - Atomic number = 23 - 11 = 12. The mass number includes both protons and neutrons, so subtracting the protons gives the number of neutrons.

questions.stem: Protons and neutrons are collectively known as:
questions.explanation: Protons and neutrons are collectively called nucleons because they are both found in the nucleus of the atom.

questions.stem: Where are electrons found in an atom?

options.text: In shells (energy levels) around the nucleus
Between the protons and neutrons in the nucleus

questions.explanation: Electrons orbit the nucleus in regions called shells or energy levels, arranged at increasing distances from the nucleus.

questions.stem: An atom of iron (Fe) has 26 protons and 30 neutrons. What is its mass number?
questions.explanation: Mass number = number of protons + number of neutrons = 26 + 30 = 56. The mass number represents the total number of particles in the nucleus.
